newsitem.title: UK: Virgin Cola complains to EC over CCSB.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Cola complains to EC over CCSB.

text.p: Virgin Cola has launched a formal complaint with the European Commission about what it sees as Coca-Cola Schweppes & Beverages' abuse of its dominant position in the UK cola market, said a company spokeswoman.
Virgin Cola, part of the Virgin Group run by millionaire entrepreneur Richard Branson, wants an investigation into CCSB's "anti-competitive practices," she said.

CCSB is currently involved with a Commission probe into the proposed 700 million stg sale by Cadbury Schweppes of its 51 percent stake in the venture to Coca-Cola Enterprises, with the findings due in January.

Coca-Cola uses schemes which offer rebates as an incentive to shops who reach certain sales targets, thereby leaving shopkeepers less inclined to stock competing brands like Virgin or Pepsi, Virgin claimed.
Discounts are also allegedly offered if a retailer will only stock Coca-Cola drinks.
Virgin also claims that other types of drink such as mineral waters may also be tied into such schemes, blocking sales not only of cola drinks.
Virgin is currently number three in terms of cola sales in the UK behind Coca-Cola and Pepsi.
